exercises.prompt: Use the pasiva refleja with *vender*: *En esta tienda ___ ___ libros antiguos.*
hints: *Se* + verb in the third person.
The verb agrees with *libros antiguos*: plural.
exercises.solution: The pasiva refleja is *se* + a third-person verb agreeing with the thing affected. *Libros antiguos* is plural, so: ***se venden***. *En esta tienda **se venden** libros antiguos* = Old books are sold in this shop.

feedback.message: Almost — in the pasiva refleja the verb agrees with the noun: *libros* is plural, so *se venden*.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the passive with *ser* (preterite) of *construir*: *El puente ___ ___ en 1890.*
hints: *Ser* in the preterite + participle.
The participle agrees with *el puente* (masculine singular).
exercises.solution: The *ser* passive uses *ser* in the required tense, here the preterite, *fue*, plus the participle agreeing with the subject: *construido* (masculine singular, like *el puente*). *El puente **fue construido** en 1890.*

feedback.message: Almost — the participle agrees with *el puente*, which is masculine: *construido*.
Not yet — for a completed event, *ser* goes in the preterite: *fue construido*.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sign: *Se ___ voluntarios para limpiar la playa.*

options.label: necesita
options.feedback: Not yet — in the pasiva refleja the verb agrees with *voluntarios*, which is plural.

options.label: necesitan
options.feedback: Yes. *Voluntarios* is plural, so the verb is plural: *se necesitan*.

options.label: necesitamos
options.feedback: Not yet — *se* goes with a third-person verb, not *nosotros*.

hints: What does the verb agree with in the pasiva refleja?
*Voluntarios* is plural.
exercises.solution: In the pasiva refleja, the thing affected is the grammatical subject and the verb agrees with it. *Voluntarios* is plural, so: *Se **necesitan** voluntarios.* (You'll see *se necesita voluntarios* on signs, but the plural is the standard form.)

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in the passive with *ser*: *Un equipo chileno descubrió la especie.* → *La especie ___ ___ por un equipo chileno.*
hints: Keep the tense: *descubrió* is preterite, so *ser* goes in the preterite.
The participle of *descubrir* is irregular, and it agrees with *la especie*.
exercises.solution: The object of the active sentence, *la especie*, becomes the subject. *Ser* takes the tense of the original verb (preterite: *fue*), and the participle agrees with *la especie* (feminine singular). *Descubrir* has the irregular participle *descubierto*, so: *La especie **fue descubierta** por un equipo chileno.*

feedback.message: Almost — the participle must agree with *la especie*, which is feminine: *descubierta*.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite with the pasiva refleja: *Analizaron las muestras en el laboratorio.* → *___ ___ las muestras en el laboratorio.*
hints: *Se* + third-person verb, keeping the tense.
Agree with *las muestras* (plural).
exercises.solution: Keep the preterite, add *se*, and make the verb agree with *las muestras*: ***Se analizaron** las muestras en el laboratorio.* This is the most common way to write a methods section in Spanish.

feedback.message: Almost — the verb agrees with *las muestras*, which is plural: *se analizaron*.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to say *You get used to everything* in general?

options.label: Se se acostumbra a todo.
options.feedback: Not yet — Spanish can't put impersonal *se* on top of the reflexive *se*.

options.label: Uno se acostumbra a todo.
options.feedback: Yes. With reflexive verbs, *uno* replaces impersonal *se*.

options.label: Se acostumbra a todo.
options.feedback: Not quite — without *uno*, this reads as *he/she gets used to everything*.

options.label: Acostumbran a todo.
options.feedback: Not yet — the third person plural refers to other people, never including the speaker, and the reflexive *se* is missing.

hints: *Acostumbrarse* is reflexive.
When *se* is already taken, which impersonal subject can you use?
exercises.solution: *Acostumbrarse* already has a *se*, so impersonal *se* would make *se se*, which is impossible. Spanish uses ***uno*** instead: ***Uno se acostumbra a todo.***

exercises.prompt: *Me robaron la bici anoche.* Who stole it, according to the sentence?

options.label: Someone unknown.
options.feedback: Yes. The third person plural without a subject refers to an unspecified person or people.

options.label: A specific group of people mentioned before.
options.feedback: Not quite — without context naming them, *robaron* doesn't point to anyone specific.

options.label: The speaker and some friends.
options.feedback: Not yet — the impersonal third person plural never includes the speaker.

hints: There's no subject. What does the bare *ellos* form suggest?
It's the Spanish equivalent of English *someone* or *they*.
exercises.solution: A third-person plural verb with no subject (*robaron*) refers to **unknown or unspecified** people. The best English is a passive or *someone*: *My bike was stolen last night.*

exercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish (use *se*): *Spanish is spoken here.*
hints: English uses a passive; Spanish prefers the pasiva refleja.
*Se* + *habla* (singular, agreeing with *español*).
exercises.solution: The natural Spanish is the **pasiva refleja**: *se* + third-person verb agreeing with *español*: ***Aquí se habla español.*** (Or *castellano*, the name preferred in some countries.) The *ser* passive, *aquí es hablado el español*, is grammatical but sounds unnatural.

feedback.message: Grammatical, but no one says it. Use the pasiva refleja: *aquí se habla español*.

exercises.prompt: How can you say *I was given a prize*? Choose all that are correct.

options.label: Me dieron un premio.
options.feedback: Yes. An active sentence with an unspecified *they* is the most natural option.

options.label: Fui dado un premio.
options.feedback: Not yet — Spanish can't make an indirect object (*me*) the subject of a passive.

options.label: Se me concedió un premio.
options.feedback: Yes. Formal, but correct: a pasiva refleja with *me* as the indirect object.

options.label: Un premio me fue dado.
options.feedback: Not quite — grammatically possible in principle, but stiff and unnatural; Spanish speakers would say *me dieron un premio*.

hints: Who is the subject of the English passive? Can that become a subject in Spanish?
Spanish needs a different structure: active, or *se*.
exercises.solution: English promotes the receiver (*I*) to subject; Spanish can't. The natural choice is an active sentence with an unspecified subject: ***Me dieron un premio***. In formal writing, ***Se me concedió un premio*** works. *Fui dado* is ungrammatical, and *un premio me fue dado* is stilted.

exercises.prompt: Use impersonal *se* with *entrevistar* (preterite): *Para el estudio ___ ___ a doscientas personas.*
hints: *A doscientas personas* has the personal *a*.
With personal *a*, impersonal *se* keeps the verb singular.
exercises.solution: Because of the personal ***a***, *doscientas personas* is an object, not a subject, so this is **impersonal se** and the verb stays **singular**: *Para el estudio **se entrevistó** a doscientas personas.* (Without *a*, with things, you'd use the plural pasiva refleja: *se analizaron doscientas muestras*.)

feedback.message: Very common, but with personal *a* the standard form keeps the verb singular: *se entrevistó a doscientas personas*.

exercises.prompt: According to the reading *Agua que viene de la niebla*, which statement is true?

options.label: Fog catchers can replace all other sources of water in the desert.
options.feedback: Not yet — the text says the fog doesn't replace other sources: it complements them.

options.label: The amount of water collected depends on the season, the wind and the altitude.
options.feedback: Yes. *La cantidad de agua depende de la estación, del viento y de la altura.*

options.label: The nets are placed horizontally on the beach.
options.feedback: Not yet — they are placed *en vertical, en lo alto de los cerros y de cara al viento*.

options.label: Fog catchers were invented in the 19th century.
options.feedback: Not yet — the text says they appeared *a finales del siglo XX*.

hints: Reread the last paragraph.
Look for *depende de*.
exercises.solution: The last paragraph says: *La cantidad de agua depende de la estación, del viento y de la altura* — option **b**. It also says the fog *no sustituye a otras fuentes de agua: las complementa* (so not **a**). The nets go *en vertical, en lo alto de los cerros* (not **c**), and they appeared at the end of the 20th century (not **d**).
